title: A Debt for the Cover
premise: Jonah Crane, a private security contractor haunted by a botched protection detail, receives a calendar invite from her handler — sent hours after his death. The invitation drops her into a live operation run by the covert network that trained her, a program that erases its failures along with their memories. As Jonah uncovers that her own missing night in Prague was an erasure, not a lapse, she must decide whether justice means exposing the network or burning it from inside. In the end she trades her clean record and her chance at a normal life to detonate the program's archive, choosing love for the one witness she was ordered to kill over the duty that made her.
about_author: Hazel Yarrow is a former risk analyst who spent a decade writing threat assessments for firms she no longer names. She writes thrillers about people whose paperwork outlives their innocence.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. Sleepless in a safehouse, Jonah guards a paranoid client while replaying the incident that broke her. At 3 a.m., a meeting invite arrives from her handler Marcus — timestamped after his confirmed death, location: tomorrow, Pier 9. She goes against every instinct. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into compulsion; grief with nowhere to sit.

chapters.title: Pier Nine
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. At the pier she finds Marcus's body staged like a training exercise and a second attendee: Elias Vann, the witness she was ordered to eliminate in Prague — alive, watching her. A dead-man's switch releases Marcus's files only if both attend. Emotional beat: vertigo; the past standing in front of her, breathing.

chapters.title: What Marcus Left
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Jonah/Elias. The files reveal 'Lantern,' the training program behind both their careers, and a purge list of erased operatives — Jonah's name flagged for Prague. Elias distrusts her; she can't prove she didn't pull the trigger on orders she can't remember. Emotional beat: uneasy alliance built on mutual suspicion.

chapters.title: The Client Nobody Trusts
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. Her current client turns out to be Lantern's finance broker, and guarding him means guarding the network's money trail. When assassins hit the safehouse, Jonah realizes her contract was bait to keep her visible and traceable. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into cold clarity — she was never the guard, always the asset.

chapters.title: Prague, Missing Hours
chapters.summary: POV: Elias. Elias walks Jonah through his reconstruction of Prague: the hotel corridor, the shot, the six hours she cannot recall. Hypnosis-adjacent memory work surfaces a fragment — her own hand lowering the weapon, someone else firing. Emotional beat: intimacy through shared damage; love beginning where interrogation ends.

chapters.title: Handlers All the Way Down
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. Following the money, they reach Deputy Director Sorrell, who offers Jonah reinstatement if she delivers Elias — the last living witness to Lantern's domestic operation. The offer is generous, which is how she knows it's an erasure order wearing a lanyard. Emotional beat: temptation of belonging versus the truth in her hands.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV: alternating. Hunted across the city, Jonah and Elias hole up and plan: Lantern's archive sits under the training facility, accessible only during a certification cycle — four days away. They count exits, bullets, and lies, and admit what they are to each other. Emotional beat: quiet before the storm; duty and desire openly at war.

chapters.title: Certification Day
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. Under cover as a returning instructor, Jonah infiltrates the facility while Elias triggers the distraction. She reaches the archive vault but finds Sorrell waiting — he expected her, because Marcus's dead-man's switch was his honeypot all along. Emotional beat: trap snapping shut; courage indistinguishable from doom.

chapters.title: Burn Protocol
chapters.summary: POV: alternating, rapid cuts. Sorrell offers Jonah the final erasure — peace, sleep, no Prague — and she refuses. Elias breaches the server room; Jonah holds the corridor against Lantern's own graduates, refusing to kill the trainees sent at her. The archive burns; Sorrell dies by his own containment protocol. Emotional beat: climax — mercy as the ultimate defiance.

chapters.title: A Debt Repaid Differently
chapters.summary: POV: Jonah. Weeks later, leaked files dismantle Lantern publicly while Jonah, officially a ghost, sleeps through a full night for the first time since the incident. She and Elias meet where Marcus died, debt acknowledged, futures unwritten. Emotional beat: resolution — justice outside the law, love chosen over duty, rest finally earned.
